the biggest thing that makes me think its not the scholar is the fact the scion is has a strong arrogance and condescension to the heroes while based upon his cards and other bits of flavor, the scholar's been more of a zen-like kind mentor figure, and even if he faded out due to the events of his promo, I don't think his personality would do a near 180.

It's hard to say what being the gateway between here and the infinite void will do to a person.

It's also no small coincidence that Guise is shown A LOT in artwork with our gateway Scholar including that crazy incap art…Lets work backwards for a second here:

Guise came into being because he is connected to Wager Master. Now, Wager Master represents all of the "impossible possibilities" of reality when "The Wager" was lost (see his bio for a stronger sense of what I'm talking about). If Wager Master (and what comes from him) represents all of the "impossible possibilities", then what represents all of the "Possible Possibilities"? The Multiverse. The Wager that nothing would happen was lost and it created the Multiverse at the begining of known time. Someone won that bet. I know because Christopher said it (sorry the link to that is in the playtester forum somewhere). Wanna know who I think won that bet? Our big bad cosmic entity. (As an aside, I still firmly believe that it was Jansa from the Enclave of Endlings who lost that initial bet. OblivAeon having a very "Endling"-like visual design doesn't help disprove that theory. There is also a comic series called Terminarc which takes place toward the end of the comic run. Coincidence?).

Ok, so I'm playing a little 6-degrees-of-kevin-bacon here with connecting Scholar to OblivAeon (if that is even his proper name), but where else exactly do you suppose a gate to the infinite void would lead if not to oblivaeon?

With that said, my money is still on Apostate (though I reserve the right to hedge any and all bets), but this is just a little something to chew on.
